narrative.intro: This ranking shows federal contract obligations by NAICS for FY2026 to date, with total obligations of $463B. Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers obligated $43.5B. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction obligated $42.8B. Aircraft Manufacturing obligated $39.1B. Engineering Services obligated $36B. Facilities Support Services obligated $32.9B. Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) obligated $32.7B. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing obligated $28.7B. Ship Building and Repairing obligated $27.1B. Computer Systems Design Services obligated $23B. Other Computer Related Services obligated $16.8B. This set of fields represents the largest NAICS markets for federal contracting so far in FY2026 to date. Readers focused on market size can use these named industries and their obligation levels to prioritize outreach, capture, or competitive analysis within the current fiscal year.

sections.heading: Which NAICS markets lead federal obligations?
sections.body: Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers obligated $43.5B. Commercial and Institutional Building Construction obligated $42.8B. Aircraft Manufacturing obligated $39.1B. Engineering Services obligated $36B.

sections.heading: How broad is the top NAICS list in dollar terms?
sections.body: The ranking lists ten NAICS markets with named obligation amounts through FY2026 to date. The ranking includes industries from insurance and construction to advanced manufacturing and computer services, with totals ranging from $16.8B to $43.5B against total obligations of $463B.

faq.q: What are the biggest federal contracting industries?
faq.a: The biggest federal contracting industries are Direct Health and Medical Insurance Carriers ($43.5B), Commercial and Institutional Building Construction ($42.8B), and Aircraft Manufacturing ($39.1B). Engineering Services obligated $36B, Facilities Support Services obligated $32.9B, and Research and Development in the Physical, Engineering, and Life Sciences (except Nanotechnology and Biotechnology) obligated $32.7B. Guided Missile and Space Vehicle Manufacturing obligated $28.7B, Ship Building and Repairing obligated $27.1B, Computer Systems Design Services obligated $23B, and Other Computer Related Services obligated $16.8B.
